sections.heading: agentAI is one platform for every laboratory robot
sections.body: A robot, drone or sensor rig is a project: its own dataset registry, its own agents, and an owner who controls both. Agents harvest, filter, label and train against that registry. Adding a robot is a configuration change.

sections.heading: Every data type and domain forms its own project
sections.body: On upload, a project returns an automatic diagnosis of its data, images or sensor logs alike, before anyone chooses a next step. The diagnosis is where the planner starts when the researcher asks what the data can support.

sections.heading: The whole path has run, from crop row to cluster checkpoint
sections.body: Every stage from a camera in a crop row to a checkpoint on the cluster has run. The dashboard and registry run on a lab server; GPU jobs queue on PSC Bridges-2. The collector and trainer are paused after a stop-loss on 2026-08-29. The supervisor is advisory and nothing it says is applied.

sections.heading: Both the Rover and the laser robot transmit data
sections.body: The Rover is a four-wheel skid-steer streaming camera, GPS and two inertial measurement units. The Laser Weed Control Robot carries two galvanometer lasers on independent channels and two cameras, one over the work zone and one forward.

sections.heading: Nothing is labelled, and that rectangle is a fixed overlay
sections.body: Nothing here is enhanced and nothing is labelled. The rectangle in the laser robot's down camera is a fixed work-zone overlay: it sits at the same pixels on frames with no vegetation in them at all.

sections.heading: Both vehicles drive our own crop plots
sections.body: Four frames off the archive, unenhanced and unlabelled, from the two vehicles that drive our own crop plots.

sections.heading: Adding the next robot takes a project, a key and a session
sections.body: A new robot needs a project, an API key and a session start. The ingest contract is the same for every vehicle and the platform does not care what the robot is. Empty projects for a mobile robot and a humanoid already sit on it, waiting for a first upload.

sections.heading: Each drive becomes a dataset at its start
sections.body: The platform registers a vehicle session as a governed dataset during the drive. Frames and sensor batches arrive over one API key. The laser robot transmits no position.

sections.heading: Two robots have put 2,686 frames on disk, none labelled
sections.body: Two robots have put 2,686 camera frames and 91,955 telemetry rows across nine streams onto the platform, over 26 drives, with 342 m of GPS track from 1,502 fixes. None of the frames is labelled.

sections.heading: Longest pass on the platform: 141 m in 213 seconds
sections.body: The longest single pass the platform holds: 141 m of track from 211 fixes, with heading from the IMU over the same 213 seconds. The platform holds 18 passes that carry position.

sections.heading: Each finished drive is diagnosed without anyone asking
sections.body: Every finished drive is diagnosed without being asked -- route, noise, cross-sensor correlation, a timeline -- for 26 live robot sessions and 45 charts so far.
sections.big_label: live drives diagnosed without being asked

sections.heading: Signed-in users drive the rover from a plain browser
sections.body: A signed-in user opens the Rover project and clicks Drive. The platform reverse-proxies the robot's own console over the lab tailnet, so the rover is driven from a plain browser with no VPN client. 1,389 joystick commands have gone through that path. Two gates sit in front of it: the platform's Google login, then the robot's own password.

sections.heading: Drive appears on the Rover project alone
sections.body: The Drive button appears on the Rover project alone, because the allow-list holds one target. The rover has been off the network since 2026-08-28, and the platform answers a drive request today with its own offline page. The laser robot has never been drivable from the platform.

sections.heading: Advisory text is the only thing the platform sends a robot
sections.body: Besides the drive relay, the platform sends a robot exactly one thing: advisory text. The rover polls for it and shows deterministic warnings about battery, current and temperature. That poll has returned 406 times. No platform code path sends an actuation command to any robot.

sections.heading: Laser on in 216 rows, with no target in any
sections.body: The laser robot's own operator switched the laser on during three of eight archived sessions. The platform recorded 3379 laser rows and 216 of them have the laser enabled. Every one of those 216 is in OBSERVATION phase, with no target. The laser has never been armed, aimed or fired by the platform.
sections.big_label: times the laser has been fired by the platform

sections.heading: Ask any dataset a question in plain words
sections.body: Every dataset page has a chat box. A planner reads the question and the data's real columns, then picks a built-in analysis or writes new code. That code runs in a sandbox with no network and no file writes, and the answer returns with its chart and code.
sections.big_label: analysis tools the planner can choose from

sections.heading: New code on the first attempt, for an unplanned question
sections.body: Asked to plot a histogram of the heading change rate on the Rover's field drive, the agent wrote the code and returned the plot on the first attempt. A fixed template cannot do that, because nothing in the platform knew that question would be asked. Across the platform, 9 datasets carry 92 turns of that conversation.
sections.big_label: questions asked of a dataset so far

sections.heading: Generated code runs fenced in, with no network and no writes
sections.body: Generated code passes an import whitelist and an AST check before it runs. It gets no network and no file writes, 15 seconds of CPU, 1.5 GB of memory and a 25 second wall clock. A user can edit the agent's code or paste their own and re-run it in the same fence.

sections.heading: None of the 92 questions was about a robot drive
sections.body: The conversational agent has answered 92 questions, and none of them was about a live robot drive. Every one of the 26 live sessions got the fixed diagnosis; not one got a question. Pointing the agent at the drives is the next thing to do and it costs nothing but asking.

sections.heading: The search ran dry after round three
sections.body: Two programs ran on the cluster unwatched, one searching for data, one training on it. They completed fifteen rounds. After the third the search found nothing new and the training set never changed, though the ledger and each round report logged new work.

sections.heading: Deciding work runs on the cluster, on open weights
sections.body: A language model decides what the collector goes after next, judges whether a candidate dataset is on topic, and reviews a finished step. Those run on the cluster, as batch jobs, on open weights. The lab box hosts only the small guide model, and a verdict produced there is marked in its own record as a draft that may not be reported.

sections.heading: Our own watchdog returned no decision on 149 dev cases
sections.body: We froze 162 real failures out of this project's own engineering record and scored every kind of supervision against them. The watchdog the loop was running returned no decision on any of the 149 dev cases. A model reading the raw artifacts reaches 0.70 recall over 116 incidents.
sections.big_label: real failures frozen as a benchmark

sections.heading: Citing evidence beats model size
sections.body: We froze 149 real failures from our own history and asked open-weight models to find them. Good reviewers cite their evidence; size matters less. Handed the twelve checks' findings, a 27-billion model found 0.149 more, a 14-billion one 0.012.

sections.heading: The corpus stopped growing at round three
sections.body: The corpus stopped growing at round three: the same 24 datasets went in every time, and the apparent growth was one staging directory nobody cleared.

sections.heading: Four of these eight turns did not work
sections.body: Four of these eight turns are things that did not work, and two are numbers this project measured and then withdrew after checking them.

sections.heading: Of 27 distinct models, one is deployed
sections.body: Thirty rows in four families, which is 27 distinct models. Five detectors trained on our own holdout, two vision models inside the loop, fourteen vision-language models zero-shot, and nine language models as reviewers. One is deployed.
sections.big_label: distinct models trained, run, or rejected

sections.heading: More harvested data measurably reduced accuracy
sections.body: The target is 0.90 mAP50-95, above the 0.869 published for this class of task. Re-initialising training rather than resuming from the previous round's weights recovers +0.0287, five times the seed spread of this recipe.

sections.heading: Firing on 25 of 2,686 frames, with no labels to check
sections.body: The deployable checkpoint draws a box on 25 of the 2,686 frames our robots recorded, and 24 of those 25 boxes are the same class. These frames carry no labels, so that is a firing rate, not recall and not precision.

sections.heading: One audited source in six clears the bar
sections.body: Label precision is measured per source against a calibrated probe. The probe reads 1.000 on the human-labelled reference set, so a source reading 0.184 is the data and not the instrument.

sections.heading: Paused since 2026-08-29
sections.body: A stop-loss paused the collector and trainer. The Rover is off the tailnet. The supervisor is advisory. None of the 2,686 frames is labelled.

sections.heading: Every mAP is a best epoch
sections.body: Most in-domain numbers are mAP50-95 on the same 1,977 images. That holdout is also the validation set during training, so every mAP here is a run's best epoch.

sections.heading: Numbers we withdrew
sections.body: 0.910 was a data leak. 0.9033 is the best of four unseeded runs; only one of the four crossed 0.90. Reading the ladder as flat is retracted.

sections.heading: Size of the thing
sections.body: One FastAPI service on a lab server carries 151 routes in its main module plus more in mounted modules. 29 people sign in with a Google account, under two roles, with a per-user grant for cluster GPU. 10 projects sit on it and two of them have a robot reporting into them.
sections.big_label: projects, two of them with a robot on the other end

sections.heading: A project starts from one sentence
sections.body: A researcher types or speaks what they want. A planning model proposes the project, its data type and the agents to staff it; the researcher corrects what it got wrong, and the project exists. Speech is transcribed by Whisper on the lab's own GPU.

sections.heading: Operators watch the detector run on the newest frame
sections.body: While a robot is driving, the project page shows its newest frame refreshing every second and a half, and the weed detector can be switched on over that frame in the same process. The operator sees what the model sees, on the drive that is happening.

sections.heading: Rates the platform holds
sections.body: The Rover samples its two IMUs, its telemetry and its control stream at 20 Hz and its GPS at 1 Hz, and sends camera frames at one per second. The Laser Weed Control Robot streams its own detections and laser state at 5 Hz and vehicle state at 2 Hz. Telemetry travels as one gzip batch per second with a sequence number, and the platform dedupes on it.

sections.heading: Where a human labels
sections.body: A member pushes a dataset's images to one of four allow-listed Roboflow projects under a per-project image budget, labels there, and pulls the labels back into the registry. Mongo holds the registry and is the source of truth; Roboflow is the labelling surface and nothing else.

sections.heading: Bugs this platform found in itself
sections.body: Until 2026-09-11 every derived GPS file on the platform was one motionless point, because the materialiser preferred the Pi's frozen fix over the board's. Reading the artifacts rather than the dashboard is what surfaced it, and 200.9 m of real track came back.

sections.heading: Moving a model between robots is one query on one registry
sections.body: Because every vehicle writes into one registry through one contract, a model trained on one robot's frames can be evaluated on another's without any new plumbing: the split is a query. So far we have only run that query across datasets, and that is the hard direction. A detector trained on 40,000 harvested images loses 0.0299 on a second weed dataset; the same eight checkpoints fall on both exams. So sharing perception between the Rover, the laser robot and whatever comes next is a measurement problem, and we have already priced it.

sections.heading: What the lab model says stays a draft
sections.body: Eight jobs need a model. Most run on the cluster; two run in the lab on a 3B model, because a person is waiting. A lab answer is marked so it cannot count as a decision: the rule about where a judgement counts travels with the answer, not with the configuration.

sections.heading: Where this goes: one platform, any dataset, any robot
sections.body: Agents will run unasked, iterate on their own output, escalate to a larger model when out of their depth, all inside a sandbox. Every capability stays in the platform after its experiment, so the next student inherits it working.

sections.heading: Capabilities land in the platform, so the next student inherits them
sections.body: Each capability is built into the platform itself and stays there after the experiment that needed it. The routing table, the ingest contract, the dataset registry, the sandbox and the scorer are all part of the product, so the next student inherits them working. That is the difference between a lab that has done an experiment and a lab that has built somewhere to do the next one.

sections.heading: Seeds matter more than architecture across three detector families
sections.body: Every in-domain number on this sheet is the same 1,977 images, held out of training and scored the same way. Five detectors were trained on it across three families. The deployable one is the smallest that kept its accuracy, at 2.6 M parameters, and the spread between families is smaller than the spread between seeds of one family.

sections.heading: Fifteen models that were never trained on weeds
sections.body: One deterministic pass each, no repeats, on the same images. The best open vision-language model reaches a fraction of the fine-tuned detector. This is the measurement that decides where a language model belongs on this platform: judging and reviewing, not detecting.

sections.heading: Test-time views buy a little and cost three passes per frame
sections.body: The deployable checkpoint, unchanged, given more views per image. Fusing without extra views buys nothing. Multi-scale with a horizontal flip buys a little and costs three passes per frame, which a robot running at 1 Hz can afford and a laser robot cannot.

sections.heading: Per-class spread beats every training change we made this year
sections.body: Per-class performance of the deployable checkpoint across the twelve species. The spread between the best and worst class is larger than every training change we made this year put together, which is why the next labels matter more than the next architecture.

sections.heading: Twelve species, one held-out image each, boxes as the model drew them
sections.body: One checkpoint, twelve held-out images, one for each species in the sealed holdout. The images were drawn one per class before the model ran, and the model ran at the confidence the laser robot deploys at. Where it fires twice on one plant or names a neighbouring species, that is on the plate too. No ground truth is drawn, so the plate shows what the detector produces and not what it should have produced.

sections.heading: Rover sends 640 x 360 frames at 1 Hz from every drive
sections.body: The Rover streams 640 x 360 at 1 Hz alongside GPS and two IMUs, and the platform files each drive as its own dataset the moment the session opens. 2,238 frames over 17 drives so far, none of them labelled.

sections.heading: The laser robot sends two cameras and no position at all
sections.body: Two cameras, one forward and one down over the work zone, arrive with laser state, vehicle telemetry and the laser robot's own detections. No position arrives at all.

sections.heading: One hypothesis held, the other was ruled out
sections.body: Both hypotheses were run as controls on round 15's exact data and seeds. The chain holds at 5.1 sigma; finishing the cosine schedule is worth -0.0058 at 1.3 sigma, inside the noise.

sections.heading: Review runs even when nothing looks wrong
sections.body: Review follows every step: failures here announced themselves as successes. Four levels by cost: the running watchdog, twelve fixed checks, a model reading files, then that model given the findings. The watchdog returned nothing on 149 frozen failures.

sections.heading: Agent Workflow Diagram
The training configuration was not the constraint
sections.body: Augmentation, replaying known species and completing labels were each tried and each left the same gap. What remains is the automatic labeller's boxes, and the audit above measures them.

sections.heading: Gemma 4 said yes to every box
sections.body: We cropped each box out and asked Gemma 4, a vision model, whether it held a weed. It said yes every time, wrong ones included, so it cannot serve as a check. Distance from trusted examples, on DINOv2 features, does the work. Fifty-one datasets were cut.

sections.heading: One bad box hides from a dataset filter
sections.body: A labelling mistake is usually one bad box in an otherwise sound picture, invisible to a whole-dataset filter. The check has to run box by box. Those tools are built, and what gating the merge on their scores is worth is the next experiment.

sections.heading: The model's explanation failed its own test
sections.body: Downloads carry no plant name, so every box from a site gets the same invented label. A model blamed that and wrote down first what would disprove it. A human approved; four runs disproved it. Web pictures average nine boxes, ours under two.

sections.heading: Under seal, the quality gate lost to raw volume
sections.body: The gate was registered against its own control before the runs, same recipe and three seeds a side, curated tier against raw tier, and the raw tier won by 0.0138. The curated tier was also four times smaller, so quality and quantity moved together and this test cannot separate them. It is on the sheet because it is the result we got.

sections.heading: 156,521 labelled by machine, 3,208 kept
sections.body: A machine labelled 156,521 pictures; 59,134 remain once duplicate downloads are removed. We audited 13,527 of them, and only 3,208 came from a source worth keeping. The checker scores 1.000 on hand-labelled pictures, so a low score means the source is poor.
